entries.title: Does the proposed lower-floor fire sequence reproduce the upper-façade free-fall interval?
entries.status: Inherited research observation or question; read its explicit limits
entries.original_record:
67. **Does the proposed lower-floor fire sequence reproduce the upper-façade free-fall interval?** NIST identifies the sustained uncontrolled fires on Floors 7–9 and 11–13, including Floor 13, while acknowledging approximately 2.25 seconds of essentially free-fall descent of the north face. This spatial separation makes the propagation and loss-of-support sequence a specific quantitative question. It does not establish a contradiction merely because the descending upper structure was above the principal fire floors.

    **The question to preserve:** Does NIST’s specified lower-floor fire damage and ensuing failure sequence actually produce sufficiently extensive loss of support, with the timing and residual forces necessary to reproduce the observed upper-façade acceleration, coherence, and motion? Relevant tests include matched model displacement/acceleration, member-force and contact histories, the failure chronology, and measurement and model uncertainty. This makes explicit the connection implicit in item 9 and historical inventory item 58.

    **NIST’s explanation and the mechanical qualification:** Upper stories need not themselves be heated to descend near gravitational acceleration if their supports fail below them. NIST attributes the interval to negligible support after lower exterior-column buckling. Compatibility with that explanation in principle does not independently validate its particular historical sequence; describing the process as progressive collapse does not replace the quantitative comparison.

    **Force constraint and observation limit:** For a defined fixed-mass body, sustained center-of-mass acceleration near gravitational acceleration requires a correspondingly small net non-gravitational vertical force. Substantial upward resistance cannot coexist with that motion unless physically justified downward forces offset it. A tracked roof point is not automatically that body’s center of mass. The body, interval, relative motion, projection, and uncertainty must be established or bounded. This limitation must be tested, not used to invent unlimited hidden motion or unexplained cancelling forces. The linked project force calculations are conditional analyses of separately identified published motion data, not an independent reproduction of NIST’s exact 2.25-second measurement or a measured historical force history. Neither the spatial separation nor free fall alone establishes simultaneous failure of every column, deliberate intervention, or a conspiracy.

    Sources: [NIST FAQ, questions 8–9 and 32](https://www.nist.gov/world-trade-center-investigation/study-faqs/wtc-7-investigation); [finite-interval force analysis](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/finite-interval-force/report.md); [roof-point and center-of-mass identifiability analysis](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/body-com-identifiability/report.md).

Reported engineering endpoint strain and local erosion strain are different quantities; the review shows that a constant cutoff’s direction of effect is not uniformly collapse-promoting. entries.status: Exact-source or applicability check still open
entries.original_record: 86. **Witness and seismic observations need source-specific timing and attribution.** **VERIFY; no substantive local seismic audit located in this reconciliation.** The supplied inventory points to [NIST Response 2020-001, sections F–G](https://www.ae911truth.org/images/PDFs/NIST-Response-2020-001.pdf) for caution concerning weak seismic signals. Preserve that as an attributed source lead until its exact language, signals, station timing, localization, and model dependence are checked. Bangs and small seismic events cannot be uniquely classified as explosions or floor failures merely by association. Weak or ambiguous signals do not prove silence, and an untested intervention is not thereby supported. Conversely, the detection-analysis limits do not erase all negative evidence against conspicuously loud scenarios: an actual absence of a predicted signal can retain conditional weight where the recording coverage and source-to-receiver applicability support detection. The [acoustic audit](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/nist-acoustic-detectability/report.md) preserves that counterweight without claiming exclusion of every mechanism. entries.original_record: 88. **Conservative modeling and historical accuracy answer different questions.** **Methodological qualification; direction and magnitude require TEST.** A choice described as conservative must identify the response, comparison, and direction for which it is conservative; that label alone does not establish fidelity to this event or justify ignoring the choice. Conversely, not every approximation weakens the model: the [connection audit’s capacity discussion](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/connection-calibration-audit/report.md) records strength-enhancing assumptions as well as omitted mechanisms. The [fracture review](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-e8a4a5e9e198fa36) likewise limits claims of a uniform collapse-promoting bias. Preserve both directions in a matched sensitivity analysis. This records the supplied introduction’s conservative-modeling versus historical-accuracy distinction, not another independent observation against fire.

The declassified Joint Inquiry, **printed p.422, footnote 1; physical PDF p.13**, places
two FBI accounts alongside one another. Its quotation of a **November 18, 2002
response, p.3**, says an equal cash deposit on the check date suggests reimbursement.
Its quotation of an **October 14, 2002 document** says there was no bank

[Joint Inquiry release](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GOVPUB-Y4_IN8_18-PURL-gpo71223/pdf/GOVPUB-Y4_IN8_18-PURL-gpo71223.pdf#page=13)

cashier's check, an equal cash **deposit**, and the $9,900 account opening, all posted
within seven minutes on February 4, 2000. It reports teller corroboration; the
reference identifying the teller interview is redacted. This is the FBI's account
of the records and corroboration, not our independent bank/teller examination.
[FBI Part 5](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040/documents-responsive-to-executive-order-14040-2-c-part-5/at_download/file#page=16)

beside these records. Neither repetition supplies the missing transaction images.
The court cites **KSA Ex91, FBI2808–09**, not plaintiffs' Ex91 (Ratchford declaration).
[OIG chapter 5, notes128–129](https://oig.justice.gov/sites/default/files/archive/special/0506/chapter5.htm)
· [2025 opinion, p.21](https://www.nysd.uscourts.gov/sites/default/files/2025-08/03-md-01570%2011182.pdf#page=21)

**Open test:** obtain both dated FBI documents, the original credit/debit ledger,
cash deposit/check images and teller statement. Equal amounts alone do not identify
the person who supplied cash. No preferred account is selected here.

The released **August 4–6, 2003 Bayoumi interview FD-302**, transcribed August 18,

deposit; the court p.21 also attributes the cash deposit to the hijackers. These
descriptions are preserved, not equated. A bank companion, cash depositor and
ultimate source of funds are separate propositions.
[News account, extracted block B056](https://www.motleyrice.com/news/september-11-2001-new-evidence-23-years-later)
· [Averment §1637, physical p.416](https://www.motleyrice.com/sites/default/files/documents/AT_HR/9-11/20240802%20Redacted%20public%20averment.pdf#page=416)

**Open test:** receipt, account-opening documents and cash-origin evidence. The
$9,900 amount alone does not establish intent to evade reporting requirements.

original_record.verbatim_published_body:
The **September 29, 2005 FBI telephone-analysis EC**, **EO14040-002752; physical p.30,
printed p.5**, places the bank visit approximately **15:30–15:40** and prints:

| Time as printed | From label | To label | Duration as printed |
|---|---|---|---|
|16:40|BAYOUMI Cell|AULAQI Home|1:00|
|16:42|BAYOUMI Cell|AR-RIBAT PAYPHONE|1:00|
|16:43|BAYOUMI Cell|AR-RIBAT FAX|1:00|
|16:52|ALTHUMAIRY (CBR)|BAYOUMI Cell|1:00|
|16:55|BAYOUMI Cell|ALTHUMAIRY (CBR)|2:00|

This is an original FBI **analysis table**, not the carrier return for those calls.
Its later discussion states that the calls' significance is unknown because their
content is unavailable. It also records Bayoumi's denial of introductions while
offering introductions as an investigative possibility.
[Table](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040/documents-responsive-to-executive-order-14040-2-c-part-5/at_download/file#page=30)

The averment §1639 calls the 16:55 destination Thumairy's **cell phone**; the FBI
table calls it **CBR**, and EO14040-002757 describes that number as a can-be-reached
number subscribed to someone else. Preserve both descriptions; the carrier and
subscriber evidence needed to map them is still missing. A fax/payphone label does
not identify a particular human speaker.
[Averment §1639/p.416](https://www.motleyrice.com/sites/default/files/documents/AT_HR/9-11/20240802%20Redacted%20public%20averment.pdf#page=416)
· [number definitions, FBI p.35](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040/documents-responsive-to-executive-order-14040-2-c-part-5/at_download/file#page=35)

**Open test:** plaintiffs Ex12A, Ex5 p.197 and their underlying Sprint/local-carrier
returns; mapping/subscriber documents, direction, timezone, billing units and
duplicate-record rules. Timing is a testable lead; conversational purpose is not
established by proximity to the bank visit.

[FBI table](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040/documents-responsive-to-executive-order-14040-2-c-part-5/at_download/file#page=35)

line; [recount_calls.py](recount_calls.py) reproduces the count from the pinned PDF.

original_record.verbatim_published_body:
The **October 28, 2001 rental-manager interview**, transcribed October 29,
**EO14040-003828–003830; supplemental1 physical pp.161–163**, describes the check as
**$775 deposit + $8 insurance + $775 rent = $1,558**. The averment §1638 instead
describes rent, security deposit and an application fee. Keep both component labels.
The interview says Bayoumi brought the check **alone**; the averment §1638 describes
him returning with both men. We have not obtained the cited later declaration and
deposition needed to compare those accounts directly.
[Interview p.2](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040/documents-responsive-to-executive-order-14040-2-c-2-d-supplemental-release-1/at_download/file#page=162)
· [Averment §1638](https://www.motleyrice.com/sites/default/files/documents/AT_HR/9-11/20240802%20Redacted%20public%20averment.pdf#page=416)

The interview also reports a roughly February 15 **$1,010** cashier's check and says
its difference from the $775 rent was unexplained to the witness. The ledger,
receipt/check images, credits and allocation are needed; the difference is not
evidence of concealed funding by itself.

Finally, the witness thought the February deposit slip/accounting ledger had been
reviewed and copied because it appeared re-stapled, with a copy in place of the
original. The FD-302 says supporting payment documents/ledgers were attached and
original copies would be maintained in the **1A section of the file**. This is an
FBI record of a witness's observation/inference, not a forensic finding of tampering
or identification of whoever handled the papers. The immediately following released
page is a January 2002 telephone-record report, not an identified payment attachment.
We have not located those attachments; their absence from that position does not
establish that they were destroyed or omitted from every release.
[Custody/attachment passage, p.163](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040/documents-responsive-to-executive-order-14040-2-c-2-d-supplemental-release-1/at_download/file#page=163)
